previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, and a tracheostomy was admitted after a fall at his nursing home. He had lower abdominal pain and a positive urinalysis, leading to a diagnosis of a complicated urinary tract infection caused by Pseudomonas. He was initially treated with ceftriaxone, then switched to cefepime based on culture results. Imaging showed no acute trauma, and his chronic leg pain was unchanged. His abdominal pain improved with antibiotics. A midline was placed for IV antibiotic administration, and his foley catheter was exchanged. He remained stable, with no respiratory decline, and completed eight days of a ten-day cefepime course by discharge. He was discharged to extended care with plans to complete antibiotics and evaluate catheter necessity.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ year old man removed GJ tube this am, inserted foley catheter
today to preserve tract, ?placement.  // ?placement

TECHNIQUE:  AP views of the abdomen were obtained before and after
administration of contrast through percutaneous gastric tube.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal radiographs ___. CT torso ___.

FINDINGS: 

The bowel gas pattern is normal. The stomach is mildly distended with air.
After injection of contrast through percutaneous gastric tube there is
opacification of the stomach and proximal duodenum without evidence of leak.

IMPRESSION: 

Expected normal opacification of the stomach and proximal duodenum via
percutaneous gastrostomy tube.

INDICATION:  History: ___ with h/o of GJ tube removal, NPO at baseline for
aspiration.  // eval acute process, transmitted upper throughout.

TECHNIQUE:  Portable supine AP chest

COMPARISON:  Chest radiographs ___ through ___.

FINDINGS: 

Endotracheal tube is in place.

IMPRESSION: 

Tracheostomy tube is in place. The lungs are normally expanded with a
background of interstitial lung disease. There is no large pleural effusion or
pneumothorax. The costophrenic sulci excluded from view. There is likely mild
pulmonary edema. Heart size is normal. The mediastinal hilar contours are
stable.

NOTIFICATION:  Mild pulmonary edema on a background of chronic interstitial
lung disease. No evidence of pneumonia.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with dislodged GJ tube now with foley tube,
please place GJ tube.

COMPARISON:  Radiographs from ___ and GJ tube exchange from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS:  Dr. ___ resident, Dr. ___,
___ and Dr. ___ radiologist
performed the procedure. Dr. ___ supervised the trainee during
the key components of the procedure and has reviewed and agrees with the
trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
100 mcg of fentanyl and 0 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 70 min during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse.
MEDICATIONS: Fentanyl, lidocaine jelly.
CONTRAST: 45 ml of Optiray
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  30.4 min, 144 mGy

PROCEDURE:  Gastrojejunostomy exchange.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
health care proxy. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and
placed supine on the exam table.  A pre-procedure time-out was performed per
___ protocol. The tube site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile
fashion.

The existing Foley catheter tube was injected with contrast and showed
opacification of gastric rugae. The Foley catheter balloon was taken down, and
a stiff Glidewire was advanced into the stomach through the tubing. The tubing
was removed, and a short-term Kumpe catheter was advanced into the stomach
over the wire. Unsuccessful attempts were made to advance the wire and
catheter into a post pyloric position following exchange of the wire for a
___ wire. The short Kumpe catheter was removed, and a 6 ___ bright-tip
sheath was advanced over the wire into the stomach. A long Kumpe catheter was
then advanced through the sheath into the stomach. The stiff Glidewire was
then successfully passed through the pylorus and past the ligament of Treitz.
The catheter was advanced over the wire into the jejunum, and the stiff
Glidewire was exchanged for ___ wire. The sheath and catheter were then
removed, and a short catheter was used to measure the stoma length. The sheath
and long Kumpe catheter were subsequently advanced into their previous
position. The ___ wire was then exchanged for a stiff Glidewire. The
catheter and sheath were then removed, and a 18 ___ 3.5 cm stoma low
profile MIC gastrojejunostomy catheter was advanced over the wire into
position.

The catheter's balloon was inflated with 7 ml of contrast diluted in sterile
water in the stomach and locked in the stomach after confirming the position
of the catheter with a contrast injection. The catheter was then flushed,
capped and secured with sterile dressings.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
complications.

FINDINGS: 

1.  Appropriately positioned new 18 ___ 3.5 cm stoma low-profile MIC
gastrojejunostomy tube.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful exchange of a gastrostomy tube for a new 18 ___ MIC
gastrojejunostomy tube. The tube is ready to use.
